generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential integers starting at 1, unique per table; never NULL. For a fresh PK, generate the next value from the current table's max key; if the row would collide with a compact row or an existing generated row, resample and continue until the row is unique. The final row count must equal table_sizes_per_instance exactly; never drop rows for PK/unique violations.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Uniformly sample an existing parent key from the final parent key set (compact rows plus generated rows that survived PK/unique filtering); never NULL for NOT NULL FK columns; 5% NULL only if the column is nullable. For unmatched_join_rows targets, reserve at least one parent key that is never sampled as a child FK (see per_column_exceptions).
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_short: Random token of 3-12 alphanumeric characters; 10% near-duplicates of an existing value (one char changed).
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_name: Random capitalized word pair from a small built-in name pool.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_address: Random house number + street word + suffix (St, Rd, Av, Blvd) + optional 'Suite ###'.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_city: Random capitalized word + suffix (ville, town, side, mouth).
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_state: Random pick from a fixed list of US states.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_status: Random pick from the enum values declared in per_column_exceptions.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_code: Random 2-10 char uppercase token; 10% near-variants of an existing value.
generic_sampling_rules.decimal_price: Uniform in [0.01, 9999.99] rounded to 4 decimals; 10% boundary values at 0.01 and 9999.99.
generic_sampling_rules.datetime: Uniform random timestamp in [2009-01-01, 2018-12-31] formatted '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'; 10% boundary at the min/max of the column's observed range.
generic_sampling_rules.distinct_share: For DISTINCT-target columns, ensure 20-50% of rows share a value with another row; verify over compact+generated rows.
generic_sampling_rules.group_sizes: For GROUP-target columns, ensure at least one group of size 1, one of size 2, and one of size >= 3; draw three distinct values from the pool and assign group sizes explicitly, then verify with a Counter over compact+generated rows.
generic_sampling_rules.rows_with_different_values: For rows_with_different_values-target columns, ensure at least two distinct non-NULL values per instance (the whole table is the group); verify after NULL planting.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_values: For comparison_boundary targets, plant the listed literal and at least one value that compares strictly on each side of the boundary (for strings, the next lexicographic string and the previous lexicographic string; for numbers, the value plus/minus one step; for dates, one day before/after) while keeping the table's date-order rules. For case-insensitive boundaries, also plant the listed variant.
generic_sampling_rules.null_planting_order: Apply the NULL rule before planting group_sizes/duplicates_for_distinct/rows_with_different_values so planted structure is not destroyed; never NULL a NOT NULL or PK column; skip NULL planting for FK columns whose spec target forbids NULL FKs.
generic_sampling_rules.unmatched_join_rows: For each targeted parent column, reserve at least one parent key that is never inserted as a child FK; all other child rows are sampled from existing parent keys. Verify after generation that every targeted parent has at least one childless row and every child FK is non-NULL and references an existing parent.
generic_sampling_rules.row_count_guard: After generating the table, verify the row count equals table_sizes_per_instance; if a row is a duplicate, regenerate PK/unique values and resample the row until the count is exact. Never drop rows.

targets.qualifying_rows: >= 2 non-NULL distinct values per instance (whole table is the group)

The rows_with_different_values target group for Products.product_price is the whole table (one grouping key per instance). The comparison_boundary target for string columns requires both 'Success' and 'success' plus a lexicographically smaller and strictly greater value; the enum list includes 'success' so the boundary is legal. table_sizes_per_instance are exact generated row counts per instance; the program must never drop rows for PK/unique violations and must ensure the final count equals the target. FK child values must be re-resolved against the final parent key set (including compact rows and generated rows that survived PK/unique filtering) before writing, and 'pragma foreign_keys = ON' must be enabled during append with a post-write 'pragma foreign_key_check'. The instance file must start as a copy of the compact database (pass the compact path into write_instance_sqlite).
